title: The Saxon Bell
summary: Someone with keys and a boat is cutting the bells loose. Pip Hobbe has smelt the Unwinder's oil on Bene't Street, under the oldest tower in the city.

intro.line: Bene't Street, after dark. The Saxon tower of St Bene't's has stood here for a thousand years. Tonight its one small bell is ringing backwards, and the ink in every shop sign is starting to run.

steps.text: Find Pip Hobbe sniffing along Bene't Street

dialogue.line: Late'un! Smell that? Unwinder's oil, that is. Stinks of the drove. All up the gutter and in at the old tower.
Corvin has been here?

reply.line: Him or his boots. Oil don't walk on its own, Late'un.
Ohh. Beeswax. You're a proper Warden, you are. Pip'll tell you everything. Nearly everything.

dialogue.line: The Sister in the tower knows. She's been in there since before the street had a name. Go on, ask her. Pip don't go near anchoresses. They stare.

steps.text: Speak to Sister Agnes Rook at the foot of the Saxon tower

intro.line: At the foot of the tower a grey shape waits, hands folded, flickering like a candle in a draught.

dialogue.line: I have kept this bell since before your city had a name for its streets. Sit. Tell me who is ringing badly.
A man with copied keys. He oils the guardians to sleep and unhooks their bells.
Then he has been in the Ink Hall. The bell-books are kept there, the record of every peal and every promise. He wanted one page.
And now the books are bleeding. Every crossed-out line in eight hundred years is crawling out. Go down to Marisol. She will be writing it all down, poor woman, instead of running.

steps.text: Meet Dr Marisol Penhaligon at the coal-hole on Bene't Street

intro.line: A coal-hole cover by the churchyard has been levered up. Lamplight and a smell of wet ink rise out of it, and a woman in a head-torch climbs out backwards.

dialogue.line: Oh, you're the Latecomer. Good. Hold still. No, not you, the imp on your shoulder. There. Gone.
Someone tore three pages out of the Saxon bell-book and the rest of the book took it badly. It's hatching. Little inky things with nibs for tails.
How many?
That's dreadful, I'll count them later. They're coming up the hole now. Mind your cuffs.

steps.text: Clear the Ink Imps boiling out of the coal-hole

intro.line: The coal-hole spits. Blots of ink unfold into grinning things with paper wings, and a soot sprite rides up the draught behind them.

dialogue.line: Splendid. Horrible, but splendid. They dissolve back into ink, did you see? I'll want a sample.
The three torn pages didn't stay here. The ink is pulling them north, past Great St Mary's, towards the Senate House. Something up there wants to be written.

steps.item: First page of the Saxon bell-book
steps.text: Pick up the first torn page in the Bene't Street gutter

travel.caption: You follow the ink trail north, past Great St Mary's, to Senate House Hill

dialogue.line: A page of vellum, the ink still wet. It lists the Saxon bell's peals by year, in a dozen hands. One line has been scratched through so hard the pen went through the skin.

steps.item: Second page of the Saxon bell-book
steps.text: Find the second page caught on the Senate House railings

dialogue.line: The second page is plastered to the Senate House railings. It is the Concord oath, the one the twelve bells swore. A thirteenth line was added later, then scraped out.

steps.item: Third page of the Saxon bell-book
steps.text: Recover the third page in Senate House Passage

intro.line: The ink runs uphill into Senate House Passage in a thin black stream, and the scratch of a pen echoes off the walls.

dialogue.line: Three pages. Laid together, the scraped line shows through: a name, and the words 'keeper of the thirteenth hour'.
Before you can read the name, every word on the pages slides off the vellum and runs away across the lawn of the Senate House.

steps.text: Defeat the Blotted Scribe before the Senate House

travel.caption: You carry the pages back down to Bene't Street and the Saxon tower

intro.line: Before the white columns of the Senate House the ink stands up: a hunched black scribe made of every crossed-out word in eight centuries of bell-books.
It dips a claw into itself and begins to write you out.

dialogue.line: The Scribe spatters across the setts and soaks away between them. The words crawl back onto the pages, meek as you like.
Far behind you, down Bene't Street, a small old bell rings the right way round.

steps.text: Return the pages to Sister Agnes at the Saxon tower

dialogue.line: There. Four of twelve, child. The Saxon bell sleeps easy, and so shall I.
The scraped line named a keeper of the thirteenth hour. The pages wouldn't let me read who.
No. Some names are struck out for a reason. Your Corvin cut his keys for the gate locks, I can tell you that much. He means to open every one.
Take my taper. It lit this tower through two plagues and a fire. It will show you the doors that do not want to be seen.
Now go up Trinity Street and listen. Something there is ticking, and it is not a clock.
